officialAdjustments.reason: Official weekly total differs from verified daily NBA player totals; no player/date correction identified.

limitations: Results use ESPN NBA regular-season box scores, including players outside the real fantasy rosters. Incomplete or mismatched scoring days are not finalized.
NBA game dates use America/New_York; matchup boundaries come from the ESPN basketball calendar, including its extended All-Star period.
ESPN statistics can be corrected after a game. Previously finalized dates require an explicit rebuild to incorporate later corrections.

Historical replay is a reconstructed prior-stat baseline, not archived preseason AI intelligence: only 2024–25 actual per-game averages drive player values. No 2025–26 outcomes, present rankings or present injuries enter those values.

The baseline date identifies when the prior NBA season had finished; the data was retrieved later. Historical player eligibility and the available player universe come from the ESPN season endpoint and may include later changes.
Daily historical roster availability is reconstructed from box-score rosters, including DNP players. Historical injury reports, waiver eligibility and announcements at lineup lock are unavailable.
Players without a complete prior-season average receive a zero baseline; rookies and other newcomers are therefore disadvantaged. This is an explicit limitation of the replay.

Actual owner roster membership, lineup slots and scoring come from ESPN historical scoring-period snapshots. Daily snapshot ownership is used; intraday transaction execution times and historical waiver queues are unavailable.

The dated player-pool API exposes current/end-of-season ownership even for historical dates. Its ownership, waiver status, rankings and injury fields are deliberately ignored; only dated actual player statistics are used.
Scheduled participants are reconstructed from dated NBA game-stat records, including explicit DNP records. Actual player production is revealed only after the simulated decisions for that date.

Players outside the archived ESPN fantasy universe cannot be drafted or acquired. When NBA team points include such players, a separate complete NBA box score must account for them and independently match every fantasy-eligible player contribution.
The seven other franchises retain their observed daily roster choices and statistics. If they later acquire an AI-held player, their recorded ownership takes priority; the conflict must be logged.
The original owner draft follows the commissioner workbook, with uniquely resolved ESPN player identities. ESPN’s offline draft import is not used for its ordering or keeper flags.

One source discrepancy is preserved explicitly: team 8, period 18 has 20 blocks in independently verified daily NBA player totals and 19 in the official ESPN weekly result. Frozen-owner period scoring uses the official 19; daily player statistics, AI-controlled scoring and future forecasts retain the verified player totals.
Post-draft experiments start with the complete actual opening roster. The common 13-player, ten-active, no-IR baseline makes explicit initial cuts when needed.

Constrained redrafts use each team’s actual owned pick positions, including its keeper slots as fresh picks. The other seven teams’ actual selections and keepers are reserved in advance; this known opponent allocation is an experiment constraint.
Seven opponents keep their recorded daily rosters and lineups. Their claims override AI ownership; forced returns can leave vacancies when the four-acquisition period budget is exhausted.

AI acquisitions are limited to four per period and one per day. Voluntary drops and newly observed opponent releases have a one-day cooldown; intraday claim order and ESPN waiver priority are not reconstructed.
The controlled team’s later actual moves are ignored. AI eligibility uses the dated opponent rosters, not final-season ownership or future claims.
Daily NBA availability is reconstructed from dated historical stat-record presence, including DNP rows. This is not an archived pregame injury or roster feed.
All AI lineups lock before the first game. Preseason estimates update 95/5 only after each completed date; no final-season player performance informs draft choices.

Regular standings and the top-four playoff bracket are recalculated. Frozen actual postseason and consolation lineups are reused even when qualification changes. Management continues through the season calendar for each controlled team.
Percentages use total makes/attempts; a category is tied if either team has zero attempts. Tied playoff series advance the higher regular seed.
Seeds use category winning percentage, then matchup wins, then stable franchise ID because a verified original draft order was not supplied.
These constrained outcomes are simulations, not causal estimates of how much an AI manager would improve an owner’s result.

Source-version discrepancy: period 18 team 8 has 20 blocks in independently verified daily NBA records but 19 in the official fantasy weekly total. A disclosed −1 owner-period adjustment preserves official frozen results. It never changes player statistics, forecasts, or the controlled team’s AI score; that comparison therefore includes this one-block difference in source versions.
